canonical.title: A First-Visit Guide to Kuching, Sarawak

siblings.title: Eat Kuching: A First-Visit Food Guide to Sarawak's UNESCO City of Gastronomy
siblings.summary: Where to eat in Kuching on a first trip: laksa legends, kolo mee, jungle-fern midin, Dayak bamboo chicken, layer cake, rooftop seafood and offbeat longhouse feasts.

siblings.title: Sleep in Kuching: where to stay with character — heritage, rainforest, longhouse
siblings.summary: Characterful Kuching stays for a first-time couple — restored shophouses in the Old Town, rainforest treehouses and design retreats around Santubong, plus longhouse and homestay nights as a base for Bako and the orangutans.

siblings.title: Do — Kuching: semi-adventurous activities & day-trips for a first visit
siblings.summary: Bako, Semenggoh and a river cruise are the unmissable trio; this is the full menu of accessible river, cave, jungle and coast activities from Kuching as a base.

siblings.title: See — Kuching: unmissable sights, icons & UNESCO World Heritage (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: Every worthwhile sight in and around Kuching — waterfront icons, cat statues, forts, museums, temples, wildlife day-trips and Sarawak's UNESCO caves — tagged by zone, touristy-vs-offbeat and must-do.

siblings.title: Offbeat Kuching: quirky finds for a first Sarawak trip
siblings.summary: Two dozen quirky, unexpected Kuching finds — oddball museums, hidden bars, weird wildlife, jungle markets and headhunter villages — each tagged by location and touristy-vs-offbeat.

siblings.title: Culture in Kuching: Museums, Festivals, Markets & Crafts — A First-Visit Guide
siblings.summary: What to see and when: Kuching's museums, dated festivals, markets and craft workshops, tagged by location and touristy-vs-offbeat for a first-time couple.

siblings.title: Around & Day-Trips from Kuching: Getting In, Out & Orbiting Sarawak
siblings.summary: Practical logistics for basing in Kuching: flights in/out, getting around on foot/Grab/river taxi, and the half- and full-day orbit of parks, longhouses, caves and islands.

sources.title: Bako National Park
sources.claim: A full day at Bako National Park for wild proboscis monkeys, bearded pigs and Sarawak's oldest rainforest.

sources.title: Semenggoh Wildlife Centre
sources.claim: Semenggoh orangutan feeding (9am & 3pm, RM10) for near-guaranteed great apes a half-hour from town.

sources.title: Choon Hui Cafe — Sarawak laksa
sources.claim: Choon Hui Cafe is the Bourdain-anointed Sarawak laksa bowl, open 7.30am and sold out by lunch.

sources.title: Sarawak River Cruise — Signature Sunset Cruise
sources.claim: Sunset river cruise, 5.30pm daily, ~RM70, with layer cake and sape music.

sources.title: Annah Rais Longhouse Day Tour
sources.claim: A day at the Annah Rais Bidayuh longhouse — bamboo architecture, 80+ families, lunch and tuak on the tanju.

sources.title: Best Time to Visit Kuching
sources.claim: Aim for April–September, with June–August the driest and the festival-heavy peak.

sources.title: Kuching climate averages
sources.claim: Kuching is the wettest city in Malaysia (~247 rainy days a year; January peaks near 660 mm).

sources.title: Best Time to Visit Sarawak — weather guide
sources.claim: Avoid the Nov–Feb northeast monsoon when boat trips and the open sea get unreliable.

sources.title: Rainforest World Music Festival
sources.claim: The Rainforest World Music Festival (26–28 June 2026) fills city and Santubong beds months ahead.

sources.title: Kuching boutique hotels
sources.claim: A characterful heritage shophouse like The Ranee runs from ~US$80/night.

sources.title: Kuching river taxi (tambang)
sources.claim: The river taxi is RM1–2 (€0.20–0.40).

sources.title: Kuching airport to city
sources.claim: Grab covers everything else, including the RM12–15 (~€3) airport run.

sources.title: Kuching iconic events & festivals
sources.claim: Etiquette: dress modestly at mosques and temples, remove shoes in longhouses, and accept the welcome tuak graciously.

sources.title: Getting around in Kuching
sources.claim: Grab thins out when you're returning from Semenggoh, Bako village or Santubong — pre-book or ask your driver to wait.

sources.title: Semenggoh Wildlife Centre — orangutans
sources.claim: Semenggoh sightings drop in the Nov–Feb fruiting season when the apes forage in the forest.

sources.title: Kuala Lumpur to Kuching flights
sources.claim: Fly into KCH via KL (~1h50, from ~€7) or Singapore on Scoot.

sources.title: Borneo Cultures Museum
sources.claim: The Borneo Cultures Museum, Malaysia's largest, RM50.

sources.title: Fort Margherita / Brooke Gallery
sources.claim: A RM1 tambang across to Fort Margherita / Brooke Gallery (RM30).

sources.title: Darul Hana Bridge & waterfront
sources.claim: The Darul Hana Bridge lit up at dusk.

sources.title: Top Spot Food Court
sources.claim: Dinner at Top Spot, the rooftop pick-your-own seafood court.

sources.title: Indigenous food in Kuching
sources.claim: Native Dayak cuisine at The Dyak or Lepau, with kek lapis layer cake to take onward.

sources.title: Kuching to Kota Kinabalu flights
sources.claim: The natural next Borneo base is Kota Kinabalu, a ~1h25 hop from ~€19.

sources.title: Fairy Cave Sarawak
sources.claim: Fairy Cave shuts Mondays, Wind Cave Tuesdays.

sources.title: Annah Rais Longhouse Adventure
sources.claim: The Annah Rais hot springs have stayed closed since Covid despite lingering in tour titles.

sources.title: Old Sarawak Museum reopening
sources.claim: The old Sarawak Museum is only partially open after long restoration delays.

sources.title: Satang Island Day Trip
sources.claim: Plan boat-dependent trips (Satang turtle islands, occasionally the Bako crossing) for May–September.
